intro.title: Union Types, Intersections & Type Guards
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user profile system that can handle different types of users, like regular users and administrators. You'll learn to use TypeScript's union types to combine multiple types into one, allowing a variable to hold different kinds of data. We'll explore intersections to merge types into a new one with all their properties, and use type guards to safely check and narrow down types at runtime. By the end, you'll understand how to create flexible and type-safe code using these fundamental TypeScript features.
intro.usecase: Union types, intersections, and type guards are essential for building robust, type-safe user interfaces in real-world applications. For example, in a dashboard with multiple widget types (charts, tables, alerts), a union type can define the possible widget data, while intersections combine common properties like `id` and `title`. Type guards then allow safe rendering—checking if a widget is a `ChartWidget` to access its `data` property or a `TableWidget` to render its `columns`. This pattern ensures compile-time safety and prevents runtime errors in dynamic UIs like admin panels, form builders, or content management systems.
